acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A representative IPv4-shaped input tokenizes to another syntactically IPv4-shaped string (four dot-separated octets in range).
AC-2: A representative hex-serial input of length N tokenizes to a hex string of the same length N.
AC-3: The same real input string, tokenized in two separate tool invocations against the same key material, produces the identical pseudonym both times.
AC-4: Two DIFFERENT real inputs never collide to the same pseudonym in a representative test set (no accidental identity merging).
AC-5: A fixture whose content would fail the DLP privacy gate is refused by the tool (not written, with a clear error), proven by a test.
AC-6: Every emitted fixture carries provenance metadata (source path, date, capability id) per C6 section 3's layout.
AC-7: SYNTHETIC/DERIVED marking only appears when explicitly requested by the caller, never inferred.
AC-8: The tool never opens a network connection or reads a credential-shaped input -- proven by a test that the tool's code path has no such call.
AC-9: The existing utils/support_bundle.py test suite (deterministic pseudonyms, exclusion of selected fixture identifiers) stays green -- the shape-preserving addition does not regress it.
AC-10: The full one-shot regression run in the foreground, awaited to completion, is unaffected outside this movement's own new files.

baseline.authority: docs/design/UI2_0_C6_CAPABILITY_EXTRACTION_CONTRACT.md section 3 (the fixture-generation procedure) and its open item 1 (exact wording: 'the tokenizer's default Tokenizer.token() hex-token shape does not by itself preserve a real identifier's original length/character class... this document requires the extraction-tooling movement to add a shape-preserving encoding on top of the existing primitive') are this movement's literal specification. Section 3.3's preserved-property checklist (address format, serial length/shape, cross-output identity equality, cluster/context membership, ordering) is the exact list this tool must prove it preserves, with a proof method per property (already named in C6 -- read and implement each one, do not invent a different list). utils/support_bundle.py::Tokenizer is the EXISTING primitive to extend, not replace (workflow section 3.1's own note: 'utils/support_bundle.py: Tokenizer provides HMAC-SHA256 pseudonyms... a useful primitive, not a complete export policy'). This is the same tokenizer already used successfully in the Private Replay Phase A slice (movement NXS-LOCAL-0027, merged) -- read that merged code for the established pattern before writing new code.

context_not_loaded: Any Java source, Gradle build, Flyway migration or Docker artefact
Actually extracting a real capability's spec/fixtures for FIRST-CAPABILITY (that is B1-5's job, using this tool)
Device contact, credentials, network access of any kind -- this tool operates on already-captured evidence directories only, never contacts a device
invariants: The tool takes an existing evidence/capture directory as input and an output directory as the C6-layout fixture set; it never contacts a device, never reads live credentials, and never runs as part of any product code path (RUNTIME-DIRECTION P-1)

Shape-preserving encoding: a tokenized value's length and character class (e.g. an IPv4-shaped string stays IPv4-shaped syntactically, a hex serial of length N stays a hex string of length N) are preserved even though the actual bytes are pseudonymized -- implement this as an addition to Tokenizer, not a parallel competing tokenizer

Cross-output identity equality: the same real identifier appearing in two different capture files (e.g. the same device's hostname in an inventory capture and a config capture) tokenizes to the SAME pseudonym both times -- this requires a stable, deterministic mapping (HMAC-SHA256 keyed, per Tokenizer's existing domain-separation model), not per-invocation randomness

Every produced fixture is marked with its provenance (source capture path/date, capability id it feeds) and passes the DLP privacy gate (utils/repository_privacy.py) before being considered ready to commit -- the tool's own test suite proves this, and the tool itself should refuse to write a fixture that fails the gate rather than silently emitting it

SYNTHETIC/DERIVED markings (C6 section 3, workflow section 3.5) are the tool's responsibility to APPLY when asked (a flag or mode), not to invent on its own -- a fixture generated from a real capture is marked as such by default; SYNTHETIC/DERIVED requires an explicit caller choice
No decision frozen in UI2_0_BASELINE_CONTRACT.md is reopened; this is an implementation of an already-specified procedure, not a new design
